messages:
maria: Heads-up: we're targeting a small canary for the quantized kernel bundle (engine v2.3-q) tonight 02:00 UTC. Plan is 5% traffic for 30m, then 25% for 30m if stable. I'm primary oncall.
vikram: ack. what's the fallback?
anya: fallback = v2.2 (non-quant) pinned. deploybot will unpin if we decide to roll forward.
maria: yes — pin v2.2 for the night and set pin-ttl 12h. If any 5xx error rate > 0.5% or latency p95 +20% vs baseline -> immediate pin rollback.
jun: can we add an automatic KV-cache warmup step? quant kernels see cold-kv variance. Suggest a 10m prewarm with synthetic prefixes on canary nodes.
tara: +1 to prewarm. I'll run the prewarm job 01:45 UTC and post logs to the release channel.
maria: good. Also watch memory growth on the quant allocator (we saw drift in last canary). If resident grows > 8% over baseline for 15m, trigger drain.
vikram: checklist for deploybot args: --bundle=engine-v2.3-q --canary=5 --canary-duration=1800 --post-canary=25 --prewarm-job=engine-quant-prewarm-2026-03-21
anya: adding deploybot note: set --pin-fallback=engine-v2.2 --pin-ttl=43200 --smoke-check=smoke/quant-smoke-v2 (includes kv integrity + sample inference)
deploybot: deploy scheduled: starting canary 5198766000 -> nodes in rg-eu and rg-us-west. Will stream events here.
sre-bot: perf baseline snapshot attached: p50=22ms p95=120ms p99=280ms error-rate=0.09% token-cost-change=+1.8%
jun: if p95 jumps > +30ms we need immediate split and pin. Also watch for tokenization mismatches: quant sometimes flips tokens around OOV margins.
tara: release notes draft: "Engine v2.3-q: quantized matmul kernels, ~2.2x throughput improvement on T4-like instances. Known issues: potential KV cold-start variance; watch mem usage." Link: https://intranet.redwood/release/engine-v2.3-q
maria: ops runbook summary I'm pasting here: 1) prewarm 01:45, 2) kick canary 02:10, 3) monitor perf + error dashboard, 4) escalate at slack #eng-oncall if thresholds hit, 5) pin to v2.2 and notify infra for rollback if pin action triggered.
vikram: who triggers the pin? automated by deploybot on threshold or manual?
maria: priority: automated pin on deploybot thresholds (error-rate or latency rules). Manual pin allowed by oncall if other signals (OOM, mem leak) show.
anya: small note: set deploybot throttle for downstream customers to avoid noisy neighbor cascades. --rate-limit=250rps/capacity-slice.
deploybot: canary start queued (ETA 02:10 UTC). Will post events: START -> HEALTH -> METRICS -> PROMOTE/ROLLOUT/PIN.
jun: I'll tail kv/cache and allocator metrics and post short updates here every 5 minutes during the window.
tara: I can cover release-notes and docs pair with SRE if anything changes during canary.
sre-bot: reminder: create a rollback incident stub before start: /incident create "engine-v2.3-q-canary-rollback" owner=maria
maria: done. Incident stub created. Everyone please pin the incident link in your browser.
vikram: small ask: if we see a small AI-quality regression (sampler mismatch), prefer partial traffic split with rerankers on fallback path rather than immediate full pin. But ops decision stays with oncall.
maria: agreed. we'll attempt staged mitigation (reroute 50% of model traffic to v2.2 for embedding-heavy routes) before full pin if it's purely quality.
anya: logging: enable extra inference sampling for first 100 responses on canary to S3 path s3://redwood-canary/engine-v2.3-q/samples/$(thread_ts)/
maria: final: I'll be in #eng-runtime 01:30->04:00. Ping me if you see anything odd. Good luck team :rocket:
